## Pre Pulse Inhibition (PPI)

-- **Duration: 20-30 minutes**   

<!-- Test description here -->
The ‘acoustic startle response’ (also referred to as the ‘startle reflex’ or ‘alarm reaction’) is an innate reflexive reaction to an intense unexpected acoustic stimulus (loud noise). In rodents the response is manifested as a rapid muscle contraction resembling a ‘flinch-like’ action. The test is used as a tool to help assess sensorimotor processing (Geyer and Swerdlow 1998). A commonly performed variation of the startle response is the ‘prepulse inhibition test’ (PPI). This consists of a weaker pre-stimulus (pre-pulse) that precedes the intense stimulus (startle pulse). The resulting effect that is generally seen is a reduced reaction to the intense stimulus (Empress Standard operating procedure). Deficits in prepulse inhibition of the startle response are typical in patients suffering from schizophrenia and other mental and neurodegenerative diseases such as autism spectrum disorders (slower habituation), obsessive compulsive disorder, Tourette's syndrome, Huntington's disease, Parkinson's disease, and Alzheimer's Disease (Valsamis et al., 2011).  

- *Empress Standard operating procedure. Title: Acoustic startle and Pre-pulse inhibition. Doc. Number: ESLIM_011_001 Rev NO. 1. Date Issued:22/02/2007*
- *Geyer MA and Swerdlow NR, Measurement of Startle Response, Prepulse Inhibition, and Habituation: Current Protocols in Neuroscience (1998) 8.7.1-8.7.15*
- *Tatiana Lipina, Viviane Labrie, Ina Weiner, John Roder. Modulators of the glycine site on NMDA receptors, D-serine and ALX 5407, display similar beneficial effects to clozapine in mouse models of schizophrenia: Psychopharmacology (2005) 179: 54–67*
- *Valsamis, B., Schmid, S. Habituation and Prepulse Inhibition of Acoustic Startle in Rodents. J. Vis. Exp. (55), e3446, doi:10.3791/3446 (2011)* 

-- **Parameters:**   

Lipina 2005: The force intensity for each trial was recorded as the startle level. The average percent reduction in startle intensity between pulse and prepulse + pulse trials at all three prepulse levels was defined as the PPI level. The percentage PPI induced by each prepulse intensity was calculated as [1-(startle amplitude on prepulse trial)/(startle amplitude on pulse alone)] × 100%. Startle magnitude in this formula was calculated as the average response to all of the P trials, excluding the first and last blocks of five P trials.

-- **Illustration:**

```{r data_loading, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

rm(list = ls())

#--------------------------- 1. Manual Entries -----------------------------#
# 1.1 INPUT FILES
file_path <- "~\\AOCF-Behavioral Tests\\PPI\\validation\\group data\\"

raw_data_file1 <- "PPI_group1_resultstable.xlsx"
raw_data_file2 <- "PPI_group2_resultstable.xlsx"
raw_data_file3 <- "PPI_group3_resultstable.xlsx"
raw_data_file4 <- "PPI_group4_resultstable.xlsx"

#---------------------------2. LOAD DATA-----------------------------#
# Load data
#raw_data1 <- read_excel(paste(file_path, raw_data_file1, skip = 1))

raw_data1 <- read_excel(paste(file_path, raw_data_file1, sep = ""), skip = 1)
data1 <- raw_data1[-1,]
data1$grs <- "gr1"
data1 <- data1 %>% 
  mutate(Animal = as.character(Anim.No.))
#raw_data <- na.omit(raw_data)

raw_data2 <- read_excel(paste(file_path, raw_data_file2, sep = ""), skip = 1)
data2 <- raw_data2[-1,]
data2$grs <- "gr2"
data2 <- data2 %>% 
  mutate(Animal = as.character(Anim.No.))

raw_data3 <- read_excel(paste(file_path, raw_data_file3, sep = ""), skip = 1)
data3 <- raw_data3[-1,]
data3$grs <- "gr3"
data3 <- data3 %>% 
  mutate(Animal = as.character(Anim.No.))

raw_data4 <- read_excel(paste(file_path, raw_data_file4, sep = ""), skip = 1)
data4 <- raw_data4[-1,]
data4$grs <- "gr4"
data4 <- data4 %>% 
  mutate(Animal = as.character(Anim.No.),
         Animal = str_replace_all(Animal, "51", "551"))

#Create data file with all cohort data
dat <- rbind(data1,data2,data3,data4)

# Load lookup data files
lookupfile <- "PPI_group_lookup_ns.xlsx"

# Read lookup data files
lookup <- read_excel(paste(file_path,lookupfile,sep = ""))
lookup <- lookup %>% 
  mutate(Animal = as.character(ID),
         grs = as.character(groups)) 

# combine exp data with lookup data
data_ppi <- full_join(dat,lookup , by= c("grs", "Animal"))

# Factor the genotype/group/sex variable 
data <- data_ppi %>%
  mutate(sex = as.factor(sex),
         grs = as.factor(grs),
         geno = as.factor(genotype)) 

```

```{r calc_PPI, echo=F, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

#-----------------------MAX G is the startle intensity ---------------------# 

#for PP trials, the force intensity for each trial was recorded as the startle level.
#Based on the Lipina 2005 protocol. 

### STEP 1 - remove the first and last Pulse trials

#remove first 5 trials and last 3 trials via the column 'No' which indexes all trials per individual
#calculate upper limit (highest No-value minus 3)
#upper_lim = range(data$No)[2]-3 # this virtually set the limit at 60 trials minus 3 (last trials)

#upper_lim = range(data$No)[2]-5
upper_lim = range(data$No)[2]-3

#Range(data$No) returns the lowest and highest value in columns ‘No’ in data. Range(data$No)[1] returns only the lowest value and range(data$No)[2] returns only the highest value (60 in this case). Therefore, actually this virtually set the limit at maximum number of trials minus 3 (last trials). 
data_red = data %>% filter(No %in% c(6:upper_lim))

### STEP 2: sanity checks on data read

# count number of pulse trials ("P120db40ms") in data
check_data = data %>% 
  filter(Trial == "P120db40ms") %>% #filter only Pulse-Trial "P120db40ms"
  group_by(Animal) %>% count() %>% rename(Pcount = n)

#count number of pulse trials 
sancheck = data_red %>% 
  filter(Trial == "P120db40ms") %>% #filter only Pulse-Trial "P120db40ms"
  group_by(Animal) %>% count() %>% rename(Pcount_redData=n) %>%  cbind(.,check_data$Pcount) %>%  rename(Pcount = ...3)
#number of pulse trials in data should be 20, number of pulse trials in reduced data schould be 10, for which animals that is not the case
Pcount_animals = sancheck %>% filter(Pcount_redData != 10)


### STEP 3 group data by ID, genotype, sex, Trial and then calculate average of RTMS, DurationMS, MaxMS and MaxG for every group 
# (i.e. every animal and every trial)  
averaged_data = data_red %>% group_by(Animal, genotype, sex, Trial, geno, grs) %>%
  summarise(av_RTMS = mean(as.numeric(RTMS)), 
            av_DurationMS = mean(as.numeric(DurationMS)), 
            av_MaxMS = mean(as.numeric(MaxMS)), 
            av_maxG = mean(as.numeric(MaxG))) #%>%

#transform column Trial into wide format
wide_av_data = pivot_wider(averaged_data, names_from = Trial, values_from = starts_with('av_')) %>% 
  #calculate the remaining startle percentage for every prepulse by dividing 
  #the average of max amplitude (av_maxG) of prepulse / average of max amplitude (av_maxG) of pulse   
  mutate(Remaining_startle_perc_PP69_20msP = 100 * (`av_maxG_PP69-20msP` / av_maxG_P120db40ms),
         Remaining_startle_perc_PP73_20msP = 100 * (`av_maxG_PP73-20msP` / av_maxG_P120db40ms),
         Remaining_startle_perc_PP81_20msP = 100 * (`av_maxG_PP81-20msP` / av_maxG_P120db40ms)) %>%
  #calculate PPI % for every prepulse by subtracting remaining startle % from 100 
  mutate(PPI_perc_PP69_20msP = 100 - Remaining_startle_perc_PP69_20msP,
         PPI_perc_PP73_20msP = 100 - Remaining_startle_perc_PP73_20msP,
         PPI_perc_PP81_20msP = 100 - Remaining_startle_perc_PP81_20msP)

#select columns and convert table back to long format in order to plot it
long_av_data = wide_av_data %>% 
  #select columns to keep
  dplyr::select(c(Animal, genotype, geno, sex, grs, PPI_perc_PP69_20msP, PPI_perc_PP73_20msP, PPI_perc_PP81_20msP)) %>%
  #convert back into long format
  pivot_longer(cols = c(PPI_perc_PP69_20msP, PPI_perc_PP73_20msP, PPI_perc_PP81_20msP), names_prefix ='PPI_perc_', names_to='Trial', values_to='PPI_perc') %>% 
  mutate(PPI_perc = abs(PPI_perc)) #take absolute values (no negative values)

## HABITUATION DATA
#create a new column 'part'. This new column is 1 for the first 5 pulse trials, 2 for the middle 10 trials, 3 for the last 5 trials
  # count number of individuals
n_ID = length(unique(data$Animal))
  # for each individual repeat 5 times 1, then 10 times 2, then 5 times 3

part=rep(c(rep(1, 5),rep(2,12),rep(3,3)),n_ID)

#filter only pulse trials and add the new column  
hab_data = data %>% 
  filter(Trial == unique(data$Trial)[1]) %>%  #filter only Pulse-Trial "P120db40ms"
  #add the new column 'part'
  cbind(.,part) %>% 
  dplyr::select(c(Animal, sex, geno, grs, Trial, part, MaxG)) %>% 
  #calculate average of maxG for each part
  group_by(part, geno, Animal, sex, grs) %>%
  summarise(av_maxG=mean(as.numeric(MaxG)))  
#  summarise(av_maxG=mean(MaxG), .groups = 'drop')

```


```{r stat_func, echo=F}

# list of gender
list_of_genders <- c("female", "male")
list_of_genders <- as.factor(list_of_genders)

# list of genotypes
list_of_genotypes <- long_av_data$geno

# list of trials
list_of_trials = as.factor(unique(long_av_data$Trial))

# list of parts
list_of_parts = as.factor(unique(hab_data$part))

# list of groups
list_of_grs = unique(long_av_data$grs)

##
# BETWEEN GENDERS WITHIN SAME GENOTYPE
stats_bgdtrials <- function(data, parameter, info_text, grouping_factor="sex") {
 
  #create a tibble to collect all stats
  stats = tibble()
  
  df <- data %>%
    rename(param = all_of(parameter),
           group = all_of(grouping_factor))    

  for (i in 1:length(list_of_trials)) {
    stat_d <- df %>%
      filter(Trial == list_of_trials[i])  
    for (j in 1:length(list_of_grs)) {
      stat_data <- stat_d %>%
        filter(grs == list_of_grs[j])
    # perform Wilcoxon Rank Sum Tests to compare between group difference
    st = tidy(wilcox.test(param ~ factor(group), stat_data, exact = FALSE)) %>%         
       mutate(method = "Wilcoxon Sum",
              variable = info_text,
              test = paste("between genders for", list_of_grs[j], "in", list_of_trials[i]), 
              sign = ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
 
  #combine stats from every iteration of the loop
  stats = bind_rows(stats, st)
    }
  }
return(stats)
}

##
# BETWEEN GENDERS WITHIN SAME GENOTYPE
stats_bgdparts <- function(data, parameter, info_text, grouping_factor="sex") {
 
  #create a tibble to collect all stats
  stats = tibble()
  
  df <- data %>%
    rename(param = all_of(parameter),
           group = all_of(grouping_factor))    

  for (i in 1:length(list_of_parts)) {
    stat_d <- df %>%
      filter(part == list_of_parts[i])  
    for (j in 1:length(list_of_grs)) {
      stat_data <- stat_d %>%
        filter(grs == list_of_grs[j])
    # perform Wilcoxon Rank Sum Tests to compare between group difference
    st = tidy(wilcox.test(param ~ factor(group), stat_data, exact = FALSE)) %>%         
       mutate(method = "Wilcoxon Sum",
              variable = info_text,
              test = paste("between genders for", list_of_grs[j], "in", list_of_parts[i]), 
              sign = ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
 
  #combine stats from every iteration of the loop
  stats = bind_rows(stats, st)
    }
  }
return(stats)
}

```

### Results 

#### PrePulse Inhibition 

```{r pl_av_PPI, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 9}

pl_av_PPI = long_av_data %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=grs, y=PPI_perc, color = grs)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NULL) +
  facet_grid (~Trial) +
  #add data-points (not overlapping)
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(dodge.width = 0.75), size = 2) +
  #define the position of the n=
  stat_n_text(y.pos = 0.5) +
  theme_pubr() +
  labs(x="",
       y="% PPI",
       title = "Average PPI per PrePulse-Trail") + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
      plot.title = element_text(vjust= 0, hjust = 0.5, size = 12)) 

#pl_av_PPI

pl_av_PPI_s = long_av_data %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=grs, y=PPI_perc, color = factor(sex))) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NULL) +
  facet_grid (~Trial) +   
  #add data-points (not overlapping)
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(dodge.width = 0.75), size = 2) +
  #define the position of the n=
  stat_n_text(y.pos = 0.5) +
  theme_pubr() +
  labs(x="",
       y="% PPI",
       title = "Average PPI per PrePulse-Trail") + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
      plot.title = element_text(vjust= 0, hjust = 0.5, size = 12)) 

#pl_av_PPI_s

#arrange the 2 plots created above into a grid with 1 rows and 2 column with automatic labelling (A,B)

Fig1
```

```{r fig1 stats}

# Stats for Figure 1 (COMPARISON BETWEEN GROUPS)

#create a tibble to collect all stats
stats = tibble()

  for (i in 1:length(list_of_trials)) {
    stat_data <- pl_av_PPI$data %>%
      filter(Trial == list_of_trials[i])
    
# perform Pairwise Wilcoxon Rank Sum Tests to compare within genotpye difference

    mutate(method = "Pairwise Wilcoxon Sum",

  }

#format the table
stats%>%
  #remove horizontal lines between rows
  kable(booktabs = T) %>%
  #prevent table from floating and scale it to page-width
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("HOLD_position","scale_down"))
```
